title: VERY thin. Good for quick mixes, but not heavy batters
text:
VERY thin. Good for quick mixes, but not heavy batters. [[VIDEOID:b1c39e9c3ed9b4477fb806459f2b707a]] It is hard to have too many mixing bowls. We don't have a dishwasher where we currently live, so I am always looking for something that will fit in our small sink and be easy to wash.

This is a set of four nested mixing bowls. In theory, they take up less room that way. Each bowl has a small handle to help keep a grip on it, and a silicone-type ring on the bottom to help the bowl not move around on your chosen surface. I really like the shades of blue as well.

Now that I have used them a while, I did notice both good and not-so-good on these. The ring is good and does help them to not slip around, but it falls off pretty easily on most of the bowls. I wish it popped into place instead of just going around the ridge.

These are VERY thin bowls. They bend very easily. If you have something heavy in them, you will need both hands to pick it up and not dump the contents. I made a cream cheese dip and almost dropped it all on the floor when I just picked it up by that side handle. These should definitely be thicker. I did a muffin batter in the largest bowl, and it bent all the time. A little frustrating.

Overall, these are fine for a spare bowl, or whipping up eggs to be scrambled. But they do not handle stiffer or heavier foods well. The plastic never feels truly clean either. I only use Dawn dishwashing soap. Even with a steel wool pad and Dawn, they still feel "greasy" to the touch. Maybe a dishwasher would take care of that, but without one, I can't answer if that would help.

So they are okay, but just okay. I will stick to my stainless steel bowls for most things, and leave these to the tinier jobs.
